title: Survivor of fatal boat crash near Squamish speaks out
summary: Spencer Seabrooke, a survivor of a fatal boat crash near Squamish, B.C., on Thursday, is speaking out about his experience. Three people died in the crash.

blocks.text: British Columbia
Spencer Seabrooke, a survivor of a fatal boat crash near Squamish, B.C., on Thursday, is speaking out about his experience. Three people died in the crash.
3 boaters died in the crash Thursday
‘Truly an accident’: B.C. boat crash survivor says his friends were trying to help people
A survivor of a fatal boat crash near Squamish, B.C., that killed three people on Thursday is speaking out about his experience.

Spencer Seabrooke said he and seven friends went out on a fan boat, also called an airboat, which he described as a flat-bottomed watercraft with a big propeller on the back that is good for shallow water.
At the time, the Squamish River had reached its highest flow in more than 20 years, according to the River Forecast Centre, after heavy rainfall over the preceding days.
A flood warning was in effect, urging people to stay away from rivers.
Seabrooke said members of the group live by the river and he knew about the warning.
"There was no white water or rolling waves or anything," he said. "Ninety per cent of the driving of the boat that we did wasn't even on the main river."
He described the flood waters in Squamish Valley as the deepest he'd ever seen.
"It was crazy."
He said the group wasn't trying to have fun or be reckless.
"Our intentions were to help others and do what we could," he said.
After a couple hours on the water, stopping at multiple locations, the boaters pulled up to a nearby creek on the east side of the Squamish River, according to Seabrooke.
Branches from a nearby tree hit the boaters, including the driver, in the face, causing "a split-second delay on hitting the throttle," Seabrooke said.
"Because of that, we drifted into the log … It turned our boat sideways, and it flipped us over."

blocks.text: Seabrooke said it was about 15 to 20 seconds between when the boat pushed off to when it flipped.
"It all happened so fast. Everybody was thrown out of the boat and sucked underneath the log and into the creek."
He said he was lucky enough to come up from under the log and not get snagged on anything. He made it to shore as quickly as he could.
"The second I got out, I just did everything I could to try to help others. I just wish I could have … done more," Seabrooke said.

He added there were enough life-jackets on board for everybody, but they didn't feel like they were at risk.
"Nobody expected to end up swimming that day."
Two women and a man died. Seabrooke describes them as wonderful people.
“It's a huge loss. And we're all … struggling with it,” he said.
Police say they are investigating the crash.
Insp. Robert Dykstra, officer-in-charge of the Sea to Sky RCMP, said to protect the integrity of the investigation, he is unable to provide any additional information.
"I appreciate there is a lot of attention on this tragic event and a desire to understand what happened. We share this sentiment," Dykstra said.
"I ask for patience while the investigative team does the necessary work to get the answers to all the questions about how and why this happened."
